en.title: Minimum Time at School After Skipping at Most K Classes
en.description:
The time spent at school on a day is the difference in hours between the latest and earliest classes attended that day, plus 1; it is 0 if no class is attended. You may skip at most K classes in total. Find the minimum total time at school over all days.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, examples, solution, and tests.
en.input: The first line contains N M K (each 1..200), followed by N lines, each a 01 string of length M.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation:
Example 1: skip either class and attend only the other, spending 1 hour at school.

Example 2: skip the only class on the second day; the first day takes 2 hours, for a total of 2.

Example 3: there are no classes, so there is no need to go to school; the answer is 0.
hints: For each day, enumerate the number of skipped classes and find the minimum width needed to cover a contiguous block of the remaining class indices; then run a knapsack over the days on the skip budget.
